981-strachan-alexander-hartley-award: Recognizes athletic leadership and academic excellence.
981-holmes-gold-medal: Since 1865, for the highest total standing in the whole curriculum.
981-wood-gold-medal: For the most outstanding clinical performance in Clerkship; not for the Holmes Medal winner.
982-medical-societies: All medical students belong to the Medical Students' Society; see p. 941.
982-undergraduate-medical-programs: See p. 940 for the Faculty. Fees are on the Student Accounts site.
982-doctor-of-medicine-and-master-of-sur: Four years, requiring a bachelor's degree. Graduates can work as supervised, undifferentiated physicians. Science and scientific method are central, through lectures, small groups, labs and computers. CACMS status: fully accredited, with probation.
Two campuses: Montreal Downtown, and Campus Outaouais in Gatineau, opened in 2020 and taught in French to a select cohort. Both share electives and residency options.

Four components: Fundamentals of Medicine and Dentistry (FMD), Transition to Clinical Practice (TCP), Clerkship, and Physicianship. Placements are bilingual or francophone, with new third-year Integrated Clerkships being developed in the RUISSS McGill network. Expect to be audio- and video-recorded, as at the Steinberg Centre.

Observation starts in first year; clerkship in third adds responsibility. Classes are in English (Montreal) or French (Outaouais), but you must work comfortably in both. French is required before admission; English proof only for those schooled in non-English countries outside Canada (p. 1001). No part-time study.

Seven years for research careers: medical sciences from September of Year 1 to December 31 of Year 2, then 3–4 years of graduate study ending in a thesis, then M.D.,C.M. from January of Year 5 to May of Year 7. Meetings every two weeks for research talk and networking.
983-doctor-of-medicine-and-master-of-sur: Six years, with Dental Medicine: an M.D.,C.M. and a Certificate in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery.
983-admission-requirements: A D.D.S. or D.M.D. from an accredited North American school, eligibility for a limited Quebec dental license (no French test first), a passed NBME Comprehensive Basic Science Exam before the deadline, and ACLS before starting.
983-application-information: Through Dental Medicine, online (postgrad Med/Dent Education), August 1 to September 1.
983-bachelor-of-science-b-sc-medicine-pr: A one-year Science qualifying program for new CEGEP graduates, then the four-year M.D.,C.M. In English in Montreal, or French in Outaouais with UQO.
983-location: Administrative Offices: 3605 de la Montagne St., H3G 2M1. Educational Services: 680 Sherbrooke St. W., Office 1701. Admissions: 2001 McGill College Ave., Suite 1310.
983-program-description: FMD covers year 1 and early year 2; TCP late year 2; Clerkship years 3–4; Physicianship all four. Objectives follow Canadian authorities. Graduates can only be licensed to practise in supervised residency, not independently.
985-program-description: Seven years, as above, meeting Thursday evenings. Taught in English. In year one you start choosing a supervisor and lab, with Research Bursaries helping you explore. By September of Year 2 pick a supervisor and department with the Advisory Committee and be accepted to graduate studies. See p. 983.
985-program-description-2: Six years, based at the Montreal General, a level-one trauma centre. MUHC handles over 802,000 ambulatory visits a year, including 134,000 emergency visits. Accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation of Canada; the M.D.,C.M. by LCME and CACMS. Taught in English. See p. 983.
985-program-description-3: For new CEGEP graduates, registered in Science with all campus services. Molecular and cell biology, metabolism, and organic chemistry if needed, plus options like computer science, chemistry, physiology and math, and required humanities, social sciences and electives.

To enter M.D.,C.M.: at least B in each compulsory course and a CGPA of 3.5. Otherwise you may be admitted with conditions, repeat a preparatory year, or be invited back after a bachelor's. Far more apply than get in, so choose a second program. Gatineau students continue in French.
986-programs-in-science-taught-by-the-fa: The Faculty teaches and collaborates on B.Sc. programs in Science (p. 1104).
986-graduate-studies-and-research-in-the: Ph.D. work in many departments, plus the M.D.,C.M. & Ph.D. (p. 985). Clinical research happens across MUHC sites, the Lady Davis Institute, the Douglas and Shriners. Several clinical departments are grouped under Experimental Medicine and Surgical and Interventional Sciences. Ask the Chair or Graduate Director.
986-graduate-training-programs-in-the-cl: Residency programs leading to McGill certificates and certification by the CMQ, College of Family Physicians and Royal College. See mcgill.ca/pgme.
987-admission-procedures-and-requirement: mcgill.ca/medadmissions wins if details differ. A rigorous, multi-criteria review guided by excellence, inclusivity, alignment, fairness and transparency. Show commitment to academics, ethics and awareness of the world you'll serve.
987-undergraduate-degree-performance: Based on degree CGPA, science prerequisites and context. Successful applicants have been above 3.5, average about 3.8; below 3.5 is rarely competitive. You may not be considered without 60 consecutive graded credits. See p. 994.
987-performance-in-the-basic-science-pre: Normally C or above. Pass or Satisfactory counts only for Winter 2020. For exemptions, contact Admissions between June and September; requests after September 30 may be ignored. See p. 994.
987-academic-context: The Committee looks at your whole record: course levels, graduate and professional study. Take challenging, varied courses with progression, and a full load in regular terms.
987-cegep-performance-for-med-p-applican: R-score generally above 34.0, average about 37.0; below 33.0 is rarely competitive. Strongest academic evidence wins out.
987-applicant-categories: Quebec's government sets places and their distribution by residence. Prove citizenship and confirm your category when applying.

Quebec Resident: University (CGPA 3.5+) or Med-P (R-score 33.0+). Canadian Out-of-Province: CGPA 3.7+. International, needing a study permit, US citizens included: CGPA 3.7+. All must meet education and science requirements, French proof and CASPer. Interviews follow ranking; final selection is by MMI within your cohort.

Your category lasts through your studies, even if status changes. Quebec requires Out-of-Province and study-permit students to sign a contract with a return-of-service obligation or a fine if they stay to practise. M.D.,C.M./Ph.D. seats come from Quebec university, Canadian and International quotas. Some seats go first to Special Pathways.
Extra positions: Quebec First Nations or Inuit through FNIFMPQ, and Quebec-resident International Medical Graduates with Advanced Standing. See p. 989.
988-file-review-process: You compete within your cohort for set positions. Files are ranked by academics, and separately CASPer, with no strict GPA line. Documents get reviewed for four to six times the number to be interviewed, such as the top 200–300 for 50 interviews. Final rank is 100% interview score. The waitlist can run until classes begin.
989-interview-process: By emailed invitation only, in two Zoom sessions, and required for admission. Virtual multiple mini-interviews use task, simulation, scenario and discussion stations based on Physicianship and CanMEDS, sometimes on sensitive themes. No clinical skills. Say at application if you want French, English or either.
Half-day sessions. Keep your date free; no repeats, and missing it for any reason ends your file. Accommodations are considered case by case.
989-process-to-request-an-accommodation-: Including colourblindness. Send the request and documents from a health professional or disability service within 3 days of your invitation or waitlist notice. Prepare ahead.
989-non-academic-qualities: Screened through CV and CASPer, then interviews, in line with CanMEDS: compassion, judgment, integrity, adaptability, creativity, respect, curiosity, reliability, teamwork, handling stress, leadership, confidence, community involvement, professionalism and personal growth.
989-special-admissions-pathways: To make classes reflect the community and include historically under-represented ethnic, cultural and racial groups, sexual minorities and all economic backgrounds.
989-quebec-first-nations-and-inuit-facul: Since 2008, twelve positions across Laval, Montréal, McGill and Sherbrooke, by preference and availability. Must be a Quebec resident with status under the Indian Act or in the Inuit registry, with R-score 28 for Med-P or CGPA about 3.2, plus education, science, French (ask about support) and Casper.

Declaring status puts you in both this and the regular contingent; otherwise regular only. Top candidates are interviewed by Indigenous and professional members. Those with a degree by July 31 apply to M.D.,C.M., perhaps with a preparatory year; others to Med-P; a bachelor's is needed for M.D.,C.M. & Ph.D.
Final selection: individual interview 50% and MMIs 50%. Confirm status with the First Nations of Quebec and Labrador Commission's coordinator. See jedeviensmedecin.com.
990-canadian-indigenous-pathway: For non-Quebec First Nations, Inuit or Métis university applicants: two of the eleven out-of-province seats. Requires formal status documents (Indian Status card, Inuit land claim recognition, or Métis National Council or Manitoba Métis Federation card), GPA 3.4, plus education, science, French (ask about support) and CASPer.

Select this in the application and upload the Indigenous personal statement. You're also assessed in the general cohort, and self-identifying is optional. An advisory committee of Indigenous faculty, students, an Elder and others reviews CV, statement, CASPer and science. You do MMIs and an individual interview; offers rest on MMI within this cohort.
The Indigenous Health Professions Program offers outreach and support. All medical students get Indigenous health teaching, with rotations available. First Peoples' House is on campus.
991-rural-and-small-populations-pathway-: For Quebec university-level applicants who did at least 3 of 5 secondary years in a public school in a rural or small area per Statistics Canada (generally under 1,000 or under 29,999 people). Two to seven seats. CGPA 3.5+. Ask about language support.

Indicate it in the application; proof of school may be requested, official only if you get an offer. Same process, but compared within the pathway and also the general pool, so a general offer frees a seat for the next person. Offers rest on MMI.
991-black-candidate-pathway: For Quebec Med-P and M.D.,C.M. candidates who self-identify as Black. No seat limit, with simultaneous general consideration. GPA 3.5+ or R-score 33.0+, Casper and CV comparable to the Quebec pool, plus education, science and French (ask about support).

A holistic review, with a personal statement read by Black community members and health professionals. Indicate it online, then submit the statement in the Portal. Joining can't harm your decision. Endorsed candidates go to MMIs; offers rest on them. The Community of Support Program offers mentorship.
992-international-medical-graduates-img-: For Quebec residents with a recognized foreign medical degree. Enter at TCP in April and earn the M.D.,C.M. Deadline November 1.

Needs CMQ Recognition of M.D. by November 1, MCCQE Part 1 and a NAC-OSCE (or LMCC), results shared via physiciansapply.ca, a Medical Student Performance Record and transcript, language proof, science and CASPer. Offers rest on MMI. Positions depend on attrition; some years none.
993-international-medical-school-graduat: Foreign medical graduates from Quebec, Canada or abroad entering year one with that degree. Needs graded transcripts, a passed MCCQE Part 1, science, French and CASPer. Offers rest on MMI. Positions depend on attrition; some years none.
Quebec-resident citizens or landed immigrants with CMQ equivalence may instead ask PGME about direct residency. Admissions: 2001 McGill College Ave., Suite 1310.
994-eligibility-requirements: The Undergraduate Medical Admissions site wins if details differ. See also Registration and Matriculation.
994-for-applicants-in-the-university-cat: For degree holders in all categories. Your degree must be a bachelor's, finished by July 31 of entry.
994-basis-of-admission-undergraduate-deg: 120 credits, or 90 from a Quebec university after a pre-university DEC, in any discipline. Full-time and on schedule, with 12–15 credits a term; up to a year extra with some part-time terms stays eligible, at the office's call. Summer is fine if regular terms are full-time. At least 60 consecutive graded credits at application.
994-second-bachelor-s-degree: Usable if the first degree qualifies, 45 new graded credits are done by the deadline, the remaining 15+ are done by July 31 at a similar level, and the second is academically stronger.
994-all-bachelor-s-degrees: Any background is welcome; study what interests you, for a broad education, not just to prepare for medicine. Degrees without grades, or narrative transcripts, aren't considered.
994-special-consideration-for-winter-202: Excluded from everyone's assessment because of COVID-19, for both GPA and full-time status.
994-eligibility-for-atypical-degrees: Multi-institution or pre-university credit: half must be done at the granting institution. Credit for informal learning, including Quebec's Reconnaissance des acquis extrascolaires, is capped at 10%.
994-basic-science-prerequisites: College or university level, with labs: Biology 6 credits, general or physical Chemistry 6, Organic Chemistry 3, Physics 6. Grades required, not Pass/Fail, except Winter 2020. Distance courses may be accepted.

Must meet a minimum grade, but aren't weighted in the GPA. Up to three may be in progress, with transcripts by May 31. Physiology, molecular and cell biology and metabolism are strongly recommended; statistics and genetics are useful.

A Levels, IB Higher Level, French Baccalaureate terminale, and AP can substitute; see mcgill.ca/transfercredit/prospective. Ask about substitutions from June to September, not after September 30. Advanced courses generally don't replace missing introductory ones.
995-eligibility-for-special-admission-pa: Pathways for those who identify as Indigenous, Black, from rural or small communities, or low-income. See Special Pathways – Underrepresented Groups.
995-requirements-for-med-p: Most finish a DEC in two years, full-time. Longer reasons include tremplin, Double-DEC, Sports-Études, medical withdrawal, course availability, or part-time terms.

Quebec residents in or graduated from: Science (200.B0, 200.B1); Double DEC (200.11, 200.12, 200.13, 200.15, 200.16); Science + IB (200.Z0, 200.Z1); Sciences, Lettres et Arts (700.A0, 700.A1); or a Quebec French Baccalaureate. DEC within three years, by July 31 of entry. You can't have applied before or been in a full-time university program.
Select this and send documents only if you took over 3 years or your results were temporarily affected.
Biology: NYA (00UK), Biology II (00XU), or new 0B01 and 0B0F; Arts & Science 01Y5, 01YJ; IB 7BL1, 7BL2; else two courses (5.32 credits).
Chemistry: NYA (00UL), NYB (00UM), Organic I (00XV), or new 0C01, 0C02, 0C0F; Arts & Science 01Y6, 01YH; IB 7CH1, 7CH2; else three courses (8.00 credits) with Organic I.
Physics: NYA (00UR), NYB (00US), NYC (00UT), or new 0P01, 0P02, 0P03; Arts & Science 01Y7 and 01YF or 01YG; IB 7PH1 and 7PH2 or 7PH3; else two courses (5.32 credits).
Math: NYA (00UN), NYB (00UP), NYC (00UQ), or new 0M02, 0M03, 0M04; Arts & Science 01Y1, 01Y2, 01Y4; IB 7MA1, 7MA2, 7MA4; else two courses (5.32 credits). Old and new codes are both accepted.
Not allowed: prerequisites outside regular terms, over a term in another post-secondary program, or graduating from another program. Grade 12 programs, including Stanstead or LCC, don't qualify.

Exceptions: a Fall DEC graduate may start a program that Winter, one term only and not counted. Past graduates never in full-time university and who never applied may apply with up to 12 credits and a letter with documents. French Baccalaureate applicants must do both years in Quebec with all compléments québécois and an R-score.
996-procedures-for-selection-and-admissi: The Undergraduate Medical Admissions site wins if details differ.
996-deadlines: M.D.,C.M., M.D.,C.M./Ph.D. and pathways: November 1. Med-P: March 1. Documents by the same dates. Submit and pay at least 48 hours before, to get your ID and password. Tests such as CASPer and MCCQE-1 must be done before the deadline.
996-notification-of-decision: Released through the online system, then by email. See the site for dates by cohort.
996-request-for-reconsideration: Very competitive: interviewed files are read by 10–20 people. Committee decisions are final. You may ask to reconsider the review procedure before interviews, or right after them before final decisions, only for an administrative error or a relevant factor you couldn't provide. Disagreeing isn't grounds.

Email Admissions within five working days of the published invitation date, or of your category's last interview day. If denied, you may go to the University Subcommittee on Admissions Review, which only checks procedure.
997-offers-of-a-position: Conditional on your bachelor's or DEC and on similar results in current studies. First offers: reply within two weeks; waitlist offers may be shorter. Accepting needs a non-refundable deposit toward fees.
997-waiting-list: You get your number, not rankings. Stay reachable and keep your details current; missing a deadline can lose the offer.
997-decision-by-proxy: If unavailable, a delegate can respond, with a written statement signed by both.
997-deferred-admission: After accepting, request in writing with documents by July 1. One year only, at the Assistant Dean's discretion. Not for Med-P.
997-transfers: No transfer places. Quebec medical students can't apply to first year for seven years from original enrolment, even after withdrawing; McGill's counts from year one, not Med-P. Students elsewhere must prove withdrawal first. Those with medical degrees or residency from Canada or the US aren't eligible; others see IMG (p. 989).

No direct Medicine–Dentistry transfers: apply to first year of D.M.D. through regular selection; see UGME Advanced Standing Policy the other way. No transfers into Med-P, and Dent-P students can't apply to the M.D.,C.M. without a degree.
998-credits-and-advanced-standing: No credit for earlier courses, except: IMG Advanced Standing (degree in 2 years); interprofessional courses other than IPEA 500 and 501; M.D.,C.M.-OMFS (2.5 years); McGill D.M.D. courses.
999-requirements-for-registration-and-ma: Some of these may be asked for during application.
999-academic-standards-and-essential-ski: You must have the intellectual, physical and emotional capacity to meet the curriculum in reasonable time, without changing its essentials. Applicants who qualify are considered, and eligible students get reasonable accommodation with Student Accessibility and Achievement, as Quebec's Charter requires.
Skills follow CanMEDS roles (Medical Expert, Communicator, Collaborator, Manager, Health Advocate, Scholar, Professional) and the Four Principles of Family Medicine.

Observe patients by sight, sound and touch; read documents; use a stethoscope, with aids if needed. Communicate well, sensitively and in writing, including non-verbal cues. Perform palpation, percussion and auscultation; ideally general and emergency care movements.

Measure, calculate, reason and solve problems promptly. Build mature relationships and work in clinics, hospitals and other settings. Show judgment, finish duties, adapt, handle uncertainty and stress. Compassion, integrity and motivation are expected.
Follow McGill's conduct rules and the CMQ code of ethics, and keep satisfactory standing. You confirm reading this when applying; it also applies through Med-P.
1000-basic-cardiac-life-support: By July 31 of your start year, show CPR level C or C+ and AED training, valid at start and kept current, from: Heart and Stroke Foundation, Canadian Red Cross, Canadian Ski Patrol, St. John Ambulance, Lifesaving Society of Quebec, American Heart Association or American Red Cross.
1000-immunization: Both campuses: a chosen professional reviews records. Submit by May 1, verified by Orientation. Meet the Protocole d'immunisation du Québec and COVID-19 directives, plus yearly flu shots; keep proof. Other vaccines may be needed.
AFMC requirements for visiting electives in third year are strongly recommended. If using your family doctor or CLSC, follow McGill's rules exactly. Missing them may mean being asked to withdraw.
1000-policy-on-students-known-to-be-infe: Carriers might not perform some procedures. If you have Hepatitis B or C, HIV or similar, you must tell the Associate Dean of UGME on entry. You're referred to SERTIH, helped with care and career advice; rotations and residency choices may be limited. Core rotation changes appear in your MSPR, and you must disclose to your residency program.
1000-health-insurance: Through the Student Society. Disability insurance: FMEQ's partner, with more from the CMA's financial division in first year.
1000-information-technology: You need a computer with office software, a browser and internet; myCourses hosts the e-curriculum. A Wi-Fi laptop is recommended, with some campus labs for backup. Applying means you agree to audio or video recording for teaching.
